text: Keep it short: five minutes a day of a lesson explained in English is enough. You are training your ear for the sounds, not trying to understand everything.
Choose slow Japanese made for learners. Watch a short video twice: once just listening, once with Japanese captions. Look up only the words you hear again and again.
Move to lessons taught in Japanese and to learner podcasts. Understanding about half is the right level. Read one easy news story a day and say it aloud.
Mix learner material with short native clips such as cooking or a one-minute news item. Use Japanese captions first; turn on English only to check what you missed.
Make native material your main diet: news, podcasts, public health pages. Listen without captions first, then with Japanese captions. Note phrases, not single words.
Follow one field closely, for example health news or a science podcast, so its vocabulary repeats. Summarise aloud what you heard in two or three sentences.
